display_long_description:
Imagine you are guiding a group in VR.

They put on their headsets and get a new set of eyes, while you stay in the real world. You are supposed to guide them in a world you are effectively blind to.

As if managing a group wasn’t challenging enough.

“Go to the left!”
“No, your other left…”
“Press that button.”
“What button?”

People get stuck, move on, or lose focus — and you don’t even see it happening.

This application gives you that visibility back.

It shows local Android-based devices (such as Meta, Pico, Samsung and AOSP) in a real-time monitoring dashboard with a grid layout.

Each device appears as a tile. You can scan all users, select one, or switch to full-screen. The interface adapts automatically and supports pagination.

Devices are automatically discovered within the local network, allowing quick setup.

The system scales with your network. In a typical subnet, up to ~254 devices can be addressed. Performance depends on bandwidth and hardware.

Running locally ensures low latency and reliable performance.

Key features:
 - Multi-device real-time monitoring 
 - Low-latency streaming 
 - Grid-based dashboard with full-screen view 
 - Automatic device discovery 
 - Network-based scalability (~254 devices per subnet) 
 - No ads 

Currently in beta, with ongoing improvements and upcoming features.
